chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Sinān and ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā together, from Ibn Miskān, from Layth al-Murādī, Abū Baṣīr, from ʿAbd al-Karīm ibn ʿUtbah al-Kūfī al-Hāshimī, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who urinates, while nothing has touched his right hand: may he put it into his wudu (ablution) water before washing it? He said: No, not until he washes it.

I said: Then if he wakes from his sleep and has not urinated, may he put his hand into his wudu (ablution) water before washing it? He said: No, because he does not know where his hand spent the night, so he should wash it.
So the proper way concerning this report is that we carry it upon a kind of recommendation, not obligation, due to the indication of the reports we have already presented.

key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendation, indicating a preferred act rather than a binding duty
key_terms.الْأَخْبَارِ: reports, meaning other hadith narrations used as supporting evidence
key_terms.وَضُوئِهِ: his wudu (ablution), meaning the water prepared for ritual purification
key_terms.يَغْسِلَهَا: to wash it, referring to washing the hand before dipping it into the water

ai.seo_question: Is washing the hand before putting it into wudu water obligatory after sleep or urination?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses washing the hand before placing it into water used for wudu (ablution), whether after urination or after waking from sleep. The closing statement clarifies that, in light of other reports, the instruction is understood as recommended rather than obligatory, making it a jurisprudential discussion in ritual purity.
